gameOver.message: Player Gem3P Vorthos is the winner

annotations.description: Playing Undercity Sewers (which enters tapped) instead of Scalding Tarn on turn 1 is a significant mistake. With Scalding Tarn, they could fetch Underground Sea (untapped), giving them access to mana on turn 1. Combined with Lotus Petal and Dark Ritual, this enables casting Orcish Bowmasters or even setting up for Quantum Riddler via Warp. More importantly, Scalding Tarn + Lotus Petal + Dark Ritual = BBB + one from petal = potential turn 1 plays. With Undercity Sewers entering tapped, they have zero mana available this turn. Additionally, having Daze in hand means they want an Island they can return — Scalding Tarn fetching an Island is better for Daze. Playing the tapped land first also means on turn 2 they'd have the Sewers untapped plus could play Scalding Tarn, but the tempo loss of not having mana available turn 1 when holding Dark Ritual and Lotus Petal is meaningful. The correct line is likely Scalding Tarn, fetch Underground Sea, then potentially cast Lotus Petal and have options open including holding up Daze with a bounceable Island.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Undercity Sewers (enters tapped) as their land for turn 1
annotations.betterLine: Play Scalding Tarn, fetch Underground Sea (untapped Island/Swamp), then cast Lotus Petal. This gives access to mana on turn 1, enables Dark Ritual lines, and provides an Island to return for Daze as a free counterspell.

annotations.description: The opponent cast Dark Ritual on turn 1, which likely enables a powerful follow-up play (possibly Orcish Bowmasters or another threat). GLM47 had both Daze and Force of Will available to counter it. Daze could be cast for free by returning the tapped Undercity Sewers to hand (it's an Island), which would counter Dark Ritual unless the opponent pays {1} (unlikely on turn 1). Force of Will could be cast by exiling Quantum Riddler (a blue card) and paying 1 life. Letting Dark Ritual resolve gives the opponent 3 black mana on turn 1, enabling explosive plays. Daze is particularly efficient here since the Undercity Sewers is already tapped and the opponent likely can't pay {1} on turn 1. The cost of bouncing the land is minimal since it enters tapped anyway and can be replayed.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to counter Dark Ritual, allowing it to resolve and give the opponent BBB mana on turn 1.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Daze (returning Undercity Sewers to hand) to counter Dark Ritual. The opponent almost certainly cannot pay {1} on turn 1, and bouncing a tapped land that enters tapped anyway is a very low cost. This prevents the opponent from making an explosive turn 1 play with 3 black mana.

annotations.description: Casting Ponder before playing Undercity Sewers is a sequencing error. Undercity Sewers enters tapped and triggers surveil 1, which would let them bin a card before Ponder. This provides additional information for the Ponder decision and fuels Murktide Regent's delve. The land enters tapped so it doesn't affect mana availability this turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Ponder before making land drop
annotations.betterLine: Play Undercity Sewers first (surveil 1, potentially binning a card to fuel delve), then cast Ponder with Underground Sea for better information and graveyard setup

annotations.description: When ordering cards for Ponder, the player chose to put Barrowgoyf on the bottom (it will be drawn first since the last chosen goes on top) and Orcish Bowmasters on top. However, the player already has two Orcish Bowmasters in hand. Barrowgoyf would likely be a better draw since the opponent has cards in the graveyard (Lotus Petal, Dark Ritual) making it immediately relevant as a threat, and the player already has redundant copies of Bowmasters. That said, a third Bowmasters could still be useful. The ordering here puts Barrowgoyf as the card drawn (first chosen = bottom of the two, which is drawn first after Ponder draws), and Bowmasters on top for next turn. Actually, let me re-read: 'last one chosen will be topmost'. So Barrowgoyf was chosen first (goes second from top), then the remaining card Orcish Bowmasters would be placed on top. Wait - there are only 2 choices and the player chose Barrowgoyf. This means Barrowgoyf goes on bottom of the two, Orcish Bowmasters goes on top. Ponder then draws a card, so the player draws Orcish Bowmasters (the topmost card). Given the player already has 2 Bowmasters in hand, drawing a third is less valuable than drawing Barrowgoyf which would be a unique threat. The player should have put Orcish Bowmasters on bottom and Barrowgoyf on top to draw Barrowgoyf.
annotations.actionTaken: Ordered cards so Orcish Bowmasters is on top (drawn by Ponder) and Barrowgoyf is underneath, drawing a third copy of Bowmasters when two are already in hand.
annotations.betterLine: Put Barrowgoyf on top to draw it, as it's a unique threat while the player already has two Orcish Bowmasters in hand. Alternatively, could have chosen to shuffle to see fresh cards.

annotations.description: Casting Consider before activating Scalding Tarn is a sequencing error. The correct line is to activate Scalding Tarn first, which shuffles the library, and then cast Consider. This way, if the top card revealed by Consider is undesirable, you've already used your shuffle effect. By casting Consider first, you surveil 1 and draw, but if the top card was bad, you've lost the option to shuffle with Scalding Tarn before drawing. Additionally, fetching first would thin the deck slightly before the surveil/draw. Furthermore, casting Consider into an opponent with an untapped Underground Sea is risky if they have Daze (though they tapped it), but more importantly the opponent could have Orcish Bowmasters which punishes the extra draw. However, the opponent's Underground Sea is tapped, so the Bowmasters concern is less immediate. The sequencing issue with fetch-before-cantrip is the main problem.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Consider with Scalding Tarn still uncracked on the battlefield
annotations.betterLine: Activate Scalding Tarn first to shuffle the library, then cast Consider from the Undercity Sewers to get a fresh look at the top card with the option of a better surveil

annotations.description: GLM47 is using Daze to counter Consider, which is a cheap cantrip. This requires bouncing an Island (Undercity Sewers or fetching first), setting back their mana development on turn 2. Daze is a valuable tempo counter that's much better used against more impactful spells. Consider is a 1-mana cantrip - trading Daze + a land drop for it is a poor exchange. The opponent has only 1 land (Underground Sea, tapped) and no cards that suggest an immediate threat. GLM47's hand contains Quantum Riddler which needs mana to cast (even with Warp at {1}{U}), and Force of Will as a backup counter for truly important spells. Bouncing their own land to counter a cantrip delays their own development significantly while the opponent loses very little.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Daze (returning an Island to hand) to counter Consider, a 1-mana cantrip.
annotations.betterLine: Let Consider resolve. Consider is a low-impact cantrip and Daze is better saved for more threatening spells. GLM47 should focus on developing their mana to cast Quantum Riddler via Warp, and hold Daze for a more impactful spell like a threat or key combo piece.

annotations.description: GLM47 is casting Daze targeting opponent's Consider. Daze costs {1}{U} if paid normally. GLM47 has Undercity Sewers (tapped) and Scalding Tarn available. To pay {1}{U} normally, they'd need to crack Scalding Tarn for an Island (paying 1 life) and tap Undercity Sewers - but Undercity Sewers is already tapped. They likely can't even pay the mana cost. Meanwhile, the alternative cost of returning an Island (Undercity Sewers) to hand is free mana-wise. Returning Undercity Sewers to hand is a real cost (losing a land drop temporarily), but paying {1}{U} when you only have Scalding Tarn untapped means you'd need to crack the fetch, losing it permanently AND paying 1 life, just to counter a Consider. The alternative cost preserves Scalding Tarn on the battlefield and only temporarily sets back the land (you can replay Undercity Sewers next turn). More importantly, countering Consider with Daze at full mana cost is a terrible trade - spending 2 mana and cracking a fetchland to counter a 1-mana cantrip, when the alternative cost lets you do it for free (just bouncing a land). This is especially bad because GLM47's hand is Force of Will and Quantum Riddler - they need lands to eventually cast Quantum Riddler or its Warp cost.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to pay the full mana cost {1}{U} for Daze instead of using the alternative cost of returning an Island to hand.
annotations.betterLine: Use the alternative cost (return Undercity Sewers to hand) to cast Daze for free, preserving Scalding Tarn. Better yet, consider whether countering Consider is even worth it - but if you're going to Daze, always use the free alternative cost in this spot rather than spending real mana.

annotations.description: Exiled Quantum Riddler (which has Warp {1}{U}, a realistic 2-mana casting cost) instead of Daze to pay for Force of Will. With only 1 land on board, Daze's alternate cost of bouncing that land is very painful, making Daze less valuable. Quantum Riddler could realistically be cast as early as turn 3 via Warp and would provide a meaningful threat plus card advantage.
annotations.actionTaken: Exiled Quantum Riddler to Force of Will, keeping Daze in hand
annotations.betterLine: Exile Daze instead, keeping Quantum Riddler as a near-term threat castable via Warp {1}{U}. With only 1 land, Daze's bounce-an-Island alternate cost is a significant setback, diminishing its value.

annotations.description: Casting Thoughtseize before playing a land for turn is a sequencing error. The opponent has only 1 card in hand, so Thoughtseize's value is limited (might whiff on a land). More importantly, by casting Thoughtseize first with Underground Sea, they use their only mana and cannot play Ponder this turn. If they had played Misty Rainforest first (getting a second land), they could have cast both Thoughtseize and Ponder, or at minimum had better mana flexibility. Additionally, playing a fetch land first before Thoughtseize lets you see the opponent's hand and then make a more informed decision about what to fetch. The correct sequence is to play a land first (Misty Rainforest), then decide on spell casting order with 2 mana available.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Thoughtseize with Underground Sea before playing a land for turn
annotations.betterLine: Play Misty Rainforest first, crack it for an Island/Swamp to have 2 mana available, then cast Thoughtseize (seeing their hand) followed by Ponder with the remaining mana, maximizing the turn's output.

annotations.description: GLM47 is using Daze to counter a Thoughtseize when they have 0 other cards in hand. Thoughtseize would resolve against an empty hand, doing nothing useful for the opponent (they'd just lose 2 life). By Dazing it, GLM47 bounces their own Island, setting themselves back on mana development for no benefit.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Daze with alternative cost (bounce Island) to counter Thoughtseize targeting an empty hand.
annotations.betterLine: Let Thoughtseize resolve. It would find an empty hand, accomplish nothing for the opponent, and the opponent would lose 2 life. GLM47 would keep their Island on the battlefield for future mana.

annotations.description: GLM47 used Daze to counter Thoughtseize when their hand was empty (Daze was the last card). Letting Thoughtseize resolve would have resulted in the opponent seeing an empty hand, discarding nothing, and losing 2 life for no benefit. Instead, GLM47 bounced their own Island, setting back their mana development for no reason.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Daze (returning Island to hand) to counter Thoughtseize with an otherwise empty hand
annotations.betterLine: Let Thoughtseize resolve. The opponent would see an empty hand, discard nothing, and lose 2 life. GLM47 would keep their land in play and maintain mana development.

annotations.description: Fetching Underground Sea instead of a basic Island leaves the player more vulnerable to Wasteland, which is one of the most common cards in Legacy. The player already has one Underground Sea in play, so a second dual land provides no additional color fixing benefit over a basic Island (which also taps for U). Having a basic Island ensures that if the opponent plays Wasteland, the player still has a land that produces mana. With two Underground Seas and no basics, a single Wasteland could be devastating, especially when the player wants to hold up Daze (which requires returning an Island to hand). The player even acknowledges Wasteland concerns in their reasoning but then fetches the dual anyway.
annotations.actionTaken: Fetched Underground Sea (a second dual land) from library.
annotations.betterLine: Fetch a basic Island to play around Wasteland while still having access to blue mana for Daze and Ponder. The existing Underground Sea already provides black mana for Orcish Bowmasters.

annotations.description: With Ponder, the player is ordering two cards on top of their library. They chose Snuff Out first (which means it goes on bottom, with Wasteland on top). Given the board state, the player has two Orcish Bowmasters and a Murktide Regent in hand but only two lands in play (both Underground Seas) and an Undercity Sewers in hand that enters tapped. Wasteland on top means they draw Wasteland this turn from Ponder. However, Wasteland is less immediately useful than Snuff Out - the opponent only has one tapped Undercity Sewers and no creatures. Snuff Out is a removal spell that can be cast for free (4 life) if they control a Swamp (Underground Sea counts). Having Snuff Out available as the draw would give them interaction against whatever creature the opponent deploys, while Wasteland only threatens the opponent's single dual land. The player should have put Wasteland first (bottom) and Snuff Out second (top) to draw Snuff Out, keeping removal available while they develop their board with Orcish Bowmasters.
annotations.actionTaken: Put Snuff Out on bottom and Wasteland on top, drawing Wasteland from Ponder.
annotations.betterLine: Put Wasteland on bottom and Snuff Out on top, drawing Snuff Out to have free removal ready while deploying Orcish Bowmasters. Making a land drop with Undercity Sewers from hand covers the land needs, and Snuff Out is more impactful given the opponent could deploy threats.

annotations.description: Casting Murktide Regent main phase into an opponent with 2 untapped lands (Island + Undercity Sewers providing U/B) when the opponent could potentially have interaction. The opponent's graveyard shows they've already used Force of Will and Daze, but casting a 7-mana threat (even with Delve) before combat and before deploying Orcish Bowmasters seems suboptimal. Bowmasters at flash speed could be held up, and playing Murktide into potential countermagic when you could instead deploy a Bowmasters (which has flash anyway) and hold up Daze protection seems risky. However, Murktide with 4 cards to exile from graveyard (Ponder, Thoughtseize, Misty Rainforest, Ponder) would cost UU + exile 4 cards for a 7/7 flyer paying just 2 mana, which is a massive threat. The opponent has already spent their Force of Will and Daze, so the coast may be relatively clear. Still, leading with the biggest threat when you could sequence Bowmasters first (or hold Murktide to protect with Daze) is debatable.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Murktide Regent delving away graveyard cards, tapping both Underground Seas
annotations.betterLine: Cast Orcish Bowmasters first (costs 1B, leaves one Underground Sea untapped for Daze backup), then deploy Murktide next turn with Daze protection available. Alternatively, use Wasteland on opponent's Undercity Sewers first to cut their mana before committing the big threat.

annotations.description: Using Wasteland now destroys the opponent's Undercity Sewers (their only non-basic land), which is reasonable tempo. However, Gem3P has two Orcish Bowmasters in hand and only 2 Underground Seas remaining after sacrificing Wasteland. Playing an Orcish Bowmasters this turn would require both Underground Seas, leaving no mana for Daze's alternate cost (no Island to bounce) or the second Bowmasters next turn without playing the Undercity Sewers (which enters tapped). The Wasteland play cuts Gem3P down to 2 lands with a hand full of spells. An alternative line is to deploy Orcish Bowmasters first (using 1U from the two Underground Seas), then Wasteland the opponent's land on a future turn or hold it as a threat. That said, destroying the opponent's dual land while they only have 2 lands is strong tempo denial, and the opponent's graveyard suggests they may be building toward a Murktide of their own. The sequencing is debatable - Bowmasters now + Wasteland later vs Wasteland now + Bowmasters later both have merits.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Wasteland to destroy opponent's Undercity Sewers, sacrificing Wasteland and going down to 2 lands.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Orcish Bowmasters first (spending UB from the two Underground Seas), then save Wasteland for a future turn when you have more lands established. This develops the board while keeping Wasteland as ongoing pressure.

annotations.description: Casting Orcish Bowmasters during own postcombat main phase instead of holding it up to cast at instant speed during the opponent's turn. Bowmasters has flash and triggers on opponent card draws - casting it on the opponent's turn (e.g., in response to a cantrip or during draw step) would potentially generate an extra damage trigger and amass trigger. The opponent is playing a cantrip-heavy deck.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Orcish Bowmasters during own postcombat main phase
annotations.betterLine: Pass the turn holding up Bowmasters + Daze with the untapped Underground Seas, then flash in Bowmasters in response to opponent's cantrip or during their draw step for extra value

annotations.description: Cast Murktide Regent before playing a land for the turn. Playing Swamp first would have left one extra untapped land after casting Murktide (4 lands, only 3 needed with full delve), and crucially would have enabled Snuff Out's alternate cost (pay 4 life) by controlling a Swamp. Casting spells before making the land drop is a sequencing error that gives up free value.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Murktide Regent using all 3 available lands and delving 4 cards, without first playing Swamp from hand.
annotations.betterLine: Play Swamp first, then cast Murktide Regent. This leaves one extra untapped mana and enables Snuff Out's alternate cost for the rest of the game.

annotations.description: Casting Orcish Bowmasters before activating Wasteland is suboptimal sequencing. By Wastelanding the opponent's Undercity Sewers first (leaving them with only 1 Island), the opponent would be less able to pay for any counterspells or interact. The player has enough remaining mana (2 Underground Seas + Swamp = 3 sources after sacrificing Wasteland) to still cast Bowmasters afterward.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Orcish Bowmasters before using Wasteland
annotations.betterLine: Activate Wasteland targeting opponent's Undercity Sewers first to cut them to 1 land, then cast Orcish Bowmasters with remaining mana from Underground Seas/Swamp

annotations.description: Allowing a second Orcish Bowmasters to resolve makes it extremely difficult to recover, as every cantrip drawn will now deal 2 damage and create 2 amass triggers. With GLM47 already behind on board and needing to cantrip to find threats like Murktide Regent, two Bowmasters essentially locks them out of their primary game plan.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to counter the second Orcish Bowmasters, letting it resolve.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Force of Will exiling Daze to counter the second Bowmasters. While this leaves an empty hand, it preserves the ability to safely cantrip when drawing into Consider/Ponder, keeping a realistic path to deploying Murktide Regent.

annotations.description: Putting Thoughtseize back on top of the library instead of the second Daze. The opponent has multiple untapped lands (Underground Sea, Swamp), making Daze easy to pay for. Thoughtseize provides hand information and guaranteed disruption, which is more valuable than a second Daze the opponent can pay through.
annotations.actionTaken: Put Thoughtseize on top of library, keeping Force of Will and two Dazes
annotations.betterLine: Put a second Daze on top instead, keeping Force of Will, Daze, and Thoughtseize. Thoughtseize provides guaranteed disruption and information, while the second Daze is diminished against an opponent with available mana.

annotations.description: Gem3P passed without taking any action in precombat main when they could play Island and cast Murktide Regent via Delve (exiling 4 graveyard cards, paying {1}{U}{U}), creating a 6/6 flyer. Combined with the existing board of ~6 power (2 Bowmasters + Orc Army token), this would represent lethal damage against an opponent at 7 life. Even without Murktide, Wasteland on opponent's Undercity Sewers would be valuable.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without playing any spells, lands, or activating abilities in precombat main phase.
annotations.betterLine: Play Island, then cast Murktide Regent (Delve 4 cards from graveyard, pay {1}{U}{U}). Then move to combat and attack with everything for lethal damage against the opponent at 7 life.
